messages:
Maya: quick question — we're seeing a few customers with corporate egress proxies that break our healthchecks and websocket streams. can we drop a short canonical guidance here (ip ranges + proxy behavior + tests)?

Erik: yep. TL;DR: prefer hostname-based allowlists + TLS passthrough/CONNECT support. if customer insists on IP allowlists, provide the published egress CIDRs (see below) and warn about rotation. also call out CONNECT for HTTPS and websocket tunnelling. :point_down:

Maya: perfect. can you list the concrete checks customers should run (squid/bluecoat/any proxy) and the minimal ports?

Erik: minimal outbound ports: 443 (HTTPS, required), 80 (HTTP, optional for redirects/health only), 5222/443 for websocket/gRPC over TLS if they inspect ALPN. we generally expect customers to allow outbound TCP 443 to our hostnames.

Erik: recommended hostname allowlist: `*.redwood-inference.com`, `api.redwood-inference.net`, and region-specific endpoints like `eu-west-1.api.redwood-inference.com`

Ashwin: if they must use IP allowlists (e.g., firewall appliance), we publish an egress CIDR bundle that is updated periodically. examples (customer-facing docs will have authoritative list):
```
203.0.113.0/24
198.51.100.0/24
192.0.2.128/26
```
Note: those are sample ranges — real ranges live in the status/egress-cidrs endpoint and are rotated for failover.

Priya: two gotchas we've hit:
- corporate proxies that terminate TLS and perform MITM (decrypt + re-encrypt) often break HTTP/2 ALPN and gRPC; they need to allow passthrough for our hostnames or at least preserve SNI and ALPN.
- proxies that block `CONNECT` to non-standard ports cause WebSocket and streaming failures. ensure `CONNECT` to port 443 is permitted.

Maya: any specific proxy configs to call out (squid / bluecoat)?

Erik: common configs:
- Squid: enable `ssl_bump` passthrough for `redwood-inference` hostnames or add `acl` + `always_direct` for those destinations. If you must decrypt, configure it to support TLS 1.2/1.3 and ALPN.
- Bluecoat/SG: add wildcard hostnames to the TLS passthrough policy or set an exception for `api.redwood-inference.*`.

Ashwin: sample tests customers can run locally (replace proxy and host):
1) TLS handshake + SNI check:
```
echo | openssl s_client -connect eu-west-1.api.redwood-inference.com:443 -servername eu-west-1.api.redwood-inference.com
```
Look for `ServerName` and `ALPN` in the output. If the proxy is terminating TLS you'll see its cert instead of ours.

2) curl via proxy (CONNECT) to test streaming/health:
```
curl -x http://proxy.corp:3128 -i -N https://eu-west-1.api.redwood-inference.com/v1/health
```
Should return a 200 and keep the connection open for streaming traces. If you get a 407 or truncated body, proxy is interfering.

3) websocket smoke test (node):
```
const WebSocket = require('ws');
const ws = new WebSocket('wss://eu-west-1.api.redwood-inference.com/v1/stream', { agent: proxyAgent });
ws.on('open', () => console.log('open'));
```
If it fails to upgrade, proxy likely blocks or doesn't support CONNECT tunnelling.

Maya: how do we communicate IP rotation to customers who can only do IP allowlist (no hostname)?

Priya: we expose two options:
- a long-lived egress CIDR bundle (documented) plus a weekly changelog and RFC-1918 style maintenance window notifications for rotations.
- a stable NAT VIP service (for enterprise/private customers) — we can allocate a small static NAT pool per tenant behind a dedicated gateway (requires dedicated/private contract).

Erik: add note on DNS TTL and caching — don't advise customers to hardcode IPs. if they do, they must refresh DNS frequently; TTLs are short (≤300s) for our API endpoints to allow rapid failover.

Maya: any extra router/firewall rules to avoid session drops?

Ashwin: two practical rules:
- allow outbound ESTABLISHED/RELATED for ephemeral high ports (1024-65535) to permit TCP SNAT return flows.
- don't aggressively NAT session timeouts; streaming can be idle for short periods but expect keepalive every ~30s; set NAT timeouts > 120s.

Erik: sample ipset/iptables snippet for customers that want to pin to our published CIDRs (Linux edge):
```
ipset create redwood-egress hash:net
ipset add redwood-egress 203.0.113.0/24
iptables -I OUTPUT -m set --match-set redwood-egress dst -p tcp --dport 443 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A OUTPUT -p tcp --dport 443 -j REJECT
```

Priya: note about HTTP/2 & gRPC — these rely on ALPN negotiation. if a proxy strips ALPN, gRPC fallbacks will fail. require ALPN passthrough or TLS passthrough for those flows.

Maya: infra-bot status check — is there an automated way to publish the canonical egress list?

infra-bot: published egress-cidrs are available at https://status.redwood-inference.com/egress-cidrs.json and via subscription to the RSS changelog. last updated: 2026-02-18.

Erik: final recommendation for support teams: when a customer reports 407/streaming failures, ask them to run the `openssl s_client` check and `curl -x` test, then request either (a) TLS passthrough for our hostnames, or (b) explicit `CONNECT` allow for port 443 and add our CIDRs to their DNS-refreshing allowlist.

Maya: awesome — I'm going to paste this into the docs PR + send an internal note to onboarding about the NAT VIP option. thanks all :pray:

Ashwin: :+1:

Erik: adding a short troubleshooting checklist to the PR now.
